title: Why Your Brain Avoids Deep Work
audience: Productivity, focus and personal development viewers
hook: You sit down to focus. Your brain suggests literally anything else.
beats: You sit down to focus.
Your brain suggests literally anything else.
One message. One tab. One quick scroll.
Suddenly, twenty minutes disappear.
Is that laziness? Not necessarily.
Distractions offer rewards you can feel immediately.
Deep work offers rewards much later.
So the first minute feels uncomfortable.
Here is how to make starting easier.
Choose one tiny, specific outcome.
Not finish the whole project.
Try write the first three points.
Put your phone somewhere you cannot reach.
Close everything except the one useful tab.
Set a timer for just ten minutes.
You are not committing to a perfect hour.
You are committing to a small beginning.
When your mind wanders, return without drama.
Each return makes the next one easier.
Focus is not found. It is practiced.
Start with ten minutes today.
